article_title: Graduation Requirements and Measures: A Review of Performance Assessment Implementation in Select States for the New York State Education Department
citation: Jenna Howard Terrell, Sarah Barzee. (2023). Graduation Requirements and Measures: A Review of Performance Assessment Implementation in Select States for the New York State Education Department. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Performance-based assessment as defined by NYSED: demonstrating knowledge by creating a response or product or doing a task, judged against rubric criteria
description: The report adopts NYSED's definition: "A performance-based assessment requires students to demonstrate or apply their knowledge, skills, and strategies by creating a response or product or doing a task." Responses or performances are judged against standards or criteria in a checklist or rubric focused on skill development stages. The report describes performance assessments as a continuum ranging from constructing a response to creating a product to performing an activity, including essays, authentic demonstrations, portfolios, exhibitions, and capstone projects.
requirements: Judging against standards or criteria in a checklist or rubric focusing on the stages of skill development and what a student can do.
constraints: The report notes there are nuances in the literature about what a performance-based assessment must entail, and the definition is adopted for the purposes of this report to NYSED.
target_learners: High school students demonstrating mastery for graduation or classroom purposes
target_learning_goals: Demonstrating and applying knowledge, skills, and strategies through products, performances, or tasks
examples: Colorado defines performance assessments as an authentic demonstration of student knowledge and skills through the creation of a complex product or presentation.
key_sources: Jenna Howard Terrell, Sarah Barzee. (2023). Graduation Requirements and Measures: A Review of Performance Assessment Implementation in Select States for the New York State Education Department. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED633310

article_title: Enhanced virtual microscopy for collaborative education.
citation: Triola Marc M, Holloway William J. (2011). Enhanced virtual microscopy for collaborative education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6920-11-4
title: NYU Virtual Microscope: an open-source, Google Maps-based virtual microscope for collaborative histology education
description: A web-based virtual microscope built on the Google Maps JavaScript API, comprising a tiling script that converts commercial slide-scanner images into 256 × 256 pixel JPEG tile pyramids and a viewer application supporting markers, metadata, free-text tags, and 'similar slides' links. The article states "this is the first implementation of VM technology using the Google Maps engine." It served 1,037 slides (682 public teaching slides, 355 exam-restricted) comprising 39,386,941 JPEG files in 349 gigabytes, with 289,352 unique slide views to date. Source code is released under the MIT License.
requirements: Freely available web server and database software (Django, MySQL; Python)
A fast Internet connection and a modern web browser for users
Institutions scanning their own slides need access to a slide scanning machine or a scanning service
constraints: Only one focal plane per slide; color correction must occur at scanning time
Digitized slides are static snapshots, so dynamic microscopic processes such as ciliary movement cannot be shown
The viewer depends on continued availability of the Google Maps JavaScript API
target_learning_goals: identification of tissue structures in histopathology
examples: Used as the sole histology viewing modality after a December 2008 pilot alongside traditional microscopes; teaching slides cover six core topic areas including General Histology (n = 436) and Parasitology (n = 71).
key_sources: Triola Marc M, Holloway William J. (2011). Enhanced virtual microscopy for collaborative education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6920-11-4
